info.name: spring-uni-api
info.description:
University Management API - full coverage.

Covers all 34 endpoints and every JPA feature that is reachable over HTTP:
- SINGLE_TABLE inheritance (courses: online / onsite)
- @ElementCollection (department contacts, PUT = full replace)
- @SecondaryTable (user profile; the user_profiles row only appears on first write)
- closed projection (GET /api/courses/summary) vs open projection (GET /api/users/display)
- soft delete: the isDeleted flag on BaseEntity and its /softDeleted endpoints
- relationships: a department lists its courses, a course lists its users, and the optional ?deleted parameter filters that NESTED list (omit it = mixed)
- MapStruct, @Version, sequences, auditing (verify these in SSMS)

- roles: a read-only catalogue over the RoleName enum, plus PATCH /api/users/{id}/role
- refresh tokens: opaque, hashed at rest, rotated on every use, with reuse detection

Run top to bottom; folders 5, 6, 7 and 8 restore every flag they set, and Cleanup removes everything it created.

item.name: 0 Auth (run this folder first)
item.description:
Registration and login. Every other folder needs the {{token}} this folder sets.

Order matters: the admin login is LAST so {{token}} ends up holding an ADMIN token, which is what the remaining folders assume.

Set the seedPassword collection variable to whatever SEED_PASSWORD your app started with, or nothing here will authenticate.

item.description:
Role is an @Enumerated entity seeded from the RoleName enum, so the catalogue is READ ONLY - there is no POST/PUT/DELETE on /api/roles and there must never be one.

The single mutating role operation lives on the user, because the user is the aggregate being changed: PATCH /api/users/{id}/role.

This folder creates its own throwaway user so it never disturbs {{userId}} or the admin {{token}}. Cleanup removes it.

item.name: 8 Refresh tokens (rotation, reuse detection, logout)
item.description:
The refresh token never travels in an Authorization header and never reaches BearerTokenFilter. It is an opaque 256-bit random string in a JSON body, stored only as a SHA-256 hash, and every /refresh call rotates it.

This folder uses its own registered user so the admin {{token}} keeps working throughout. Cleanup removes it.
